construction_note: raw_id widened i64->u64 (2026-07-27): observed vLLM block hashes routinely exceed i64::MAX. The byte encoding is unchanged -- big-endian eight bytes -- so every pseudonym below is bit-for-bit what the i64 form produced. The two rows that were negative are relabelled to the u64 with the identical bit pattern; no value was recomputed. The content-id context pins the SECOND identity space: a content_id is derived from what a block contains and is comparable across the fleet, while a block_id is the engine's and is comparable only inside the process that computed it. They are mapped under different contexts so the two cannot be joined by accident -- the vectors below share raw ids with the block-id vectors and yield different pseudonyms, which is that separation stated as data rather than as prose.
